items.a: Anacan is a mobile app that tracks your menstrual cycle, pregnancy and motherhood journey in one place. Flow mode gives you a period calendar and ovulation predictions, Bump mode follows your pregnancy across all 40 weeks, Mommy mode logs your baby's sleep, feeding and growth, and Partner mode brings dads into the journey. The app includes 30+ tools, a 24/7 Anacan.AI assistant, a community of mothers and expert content.

Yes. You can download Anacan for free and use the core tools — cycle calendar, weekly pregnancy tracker, counters and logs — at no cost. A Premium subscription unlocks extras like unlimited Anacan.AI chat, weekly PDF reports, AI photoshoots and an ad-free experience.

Anacan currently works in 5 languages: Azerbaijani, English, Russian, Turkish and Kazakh. All app content — tools, daily tips and Anacan.AI answers — is delivered in the language you choose. New languages are added regularly.

Anacan.AI provides general, science-based information, but it does not diagnose and does not replace a doctor's visit. In urgent or worrying situations, always contact your doctor. The in-app "Danger signs" guide shows exactly when you should seek immediate care.

Yes. Your health data is stored encrypted, never sold to third parties and never shared for advertising. You can delete your account and all your data directly from the app at any time. See our Privacy Policy for details.

items.q: Which devices does Anacan run on?
items.a: Anacan runs on iPhone with iOS 15 or newer and Android phones with Android 8.0 or newer. You can download it free from the App Store and Google Play.

faq.q: How accurate are cycle predictions?
faq.a: Predictions are based on the data you log and get sharper each cycle. For irregular cycles, the app accounts for variability and shows a wider window. Predictions are not a form of contraception.

faq.q: How is the ovulation window calculated?
faq.a: From your average cycle length and logged symptoms, using standard luteal-phase assumptions. For precise timing, you can pair it with ovulation test strips.

faq.q: Who can see my cycle data?
faq.a: No one. Your cycle data is encrypted, never used for advertising and fully deletable whenever you choose.

faq.q: How is my due date calculated?
faq.a: With the standard Naegele rule: first day of your last period + 280 days. If your ultrasound date differs, enter it — all content adapts to the new date.

faq.q: When should I start using the kick counter?
faq.a: Daily tracking is usually recommended from week 28. If you notice a clear decrease in your baby's movements, contact your doctor immediately.

faq.q: What is the 5-1-1 rule in the contraction timer?
faq.a: If contractions come every 5 minutes, last 1 minute each, and this continues for 1 hour — it's time to go to the hospital. The timer tracks this automatically.

aboutPage.story2: So we merged what used to take four separate apps — a cycle tracker, a pregnancy calendar, a baby log and a dad guide — into one superapp, and added an AI assistant that works around the clock.
aboutPage.story3: Today Anacan is part of daily life for thousands of families in 5 languages with 30+ tools — and this is only the beginning.

items.q: What is Anacan and who is it for?
items.a: Anacan is a superapp that tracks the menstrual cycle, pregnancy and motherhood in one place. It's built for women tracking their cycle, expecting mothers, new moms and dads who want to support them. Four modes (Flow, Bump, Mommy, Partner) adapt to your stage of life.

Yes — downloading and the core tools are completely free: cycle calendar, weekly pregnancy guide, counters, logs, community and daily content. Premium is only for extras (unlimited AI, PDF reports, AI photos).
Currently 5: Azerbaijani, English, Russian, Turkish and Kazakh. Switch anytime inside the app — all content, tools and AI answers follow your chosen language.

items.q: How does Anacan.AI work and what does it answer?
items.a: Anacan.AI takes your stage into account (cycle day, pregnancy week, baby's age) and gives science-based answers on pregnancy, baby care, nutrition and safety. It doesn't diagnose — for serious concerns it directs you to a doctor.
Health data is stored encrypted, never sold to third parties and never used for ad targeting. You can delete your account and all data directly in the app. Details: Privacy Policy.
iPhone (iOS 15+) and Android (8.0+). Find "Anacan" on the App Store and Google Play.
The mother sends an invite code from her app; the partner downloads Anacan and enters the code. Once paired, the partner receives live updates, the daily summary and SOS alerts.

items.q: Can cycle predictions be used as contraception?
items.a: No. Predictions are informational and not a contraceptive method. Discuss suitable family-planning methods with your doctor.

items.q: From which week can I start tracking pregnancy?
items.a: Any week. Enter your last period date or the ultrasound due date — the app calculates your current week and adapts all content.

items.q: Can I track more than one child?
items.a: Yes, Mommy mode supports a separate profile per child. You can even track a pregnancy and an existing baby in parallel.
App Store: Settings → Apple ID → Subscriptions. Google Play: Profile → Payments & subscriptions. After cancelling, Premium stays active until the end of the paid period.

items.q: How do I delete my account and data?
items.a: In the app: Profile → Settings → Delete account. This permanently removes all your personal data from our servers. Questions? Write to info@anacan.az.

legalPrivacy.title: Privacy Policy
legalPrivacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how Anacan LLC ("Anacan", "we") collects, uses and protects your data through the Anacan mobile app and the anacan.az website. By using the service you agree to this policy.

sections.p: Account data (name, email), the health records you enter (cycle dates, pregnancy week, baby logs, symptoms), device data (model, OS, language) and anonymized usage statistics.
We use your data only to provide the service: personal predictions, stage-appropriate content, AI answers and technical support. We do not sell your data to advertisers.
Your health records are treated as special-category data and processed only with your explicit consent. They are stored encrypted and never used for ad targeting.
Data is stored on servers protected with modern encryption standards. Transport is TLS-encrypted. We keep data only as long as needed to provide the service.
We rely on trusted infrastructure partners (hosting, analytics, payment processing, push notifications). These partners process data only on our instructions under contract.
You may request access, correction, export or complete deletion of your data at any time. Account deletion is available in the app's Settings; for requests, write to info@anacan.az.
Anacan is intended for users aged 16 and older. Records that parents keep about their babies remain under the parent's control and are protected by the rules above.
If this policy changes materially, we notify you in the app and on this page. Continued use means acceptance of the updated policy.
For privacy questions: info@anacan.az · Anacan LLC, Baku, Azerbaijan.

ovulationPage.title: Ovulation Calculator
ovulationPage.subtitle: Enter the date of your last period — find your fertile window and the days with the highest chance of conceiving in seconds.
ovulationPage.formLastPeriod: First day of your last period
ovulationPage.formCycleLengthHint: Typically 21–35 days for most women (28 on average)
ovulationPage.resultNote: These days carry the highest chance of conceiving.
ovulationPage.errorMsg: Please select the date of your last period.
ovulationPage.intro: Ovulation is the moment a mature egg is released from the ovary — the most fertile stretch of the month for conceiving. The calculator below estimates your fertile window from the date of your last period and your average cycle length.
ovulationPage.howText: The calculation uses the calendar method: the luteal phase (the stretch from ovulation to the next period) is fairly stable for most women — about 14 days. The calculator counts back 14 days from your next expected period to estimate ovulation day, then sets the fertile window from 5 days before that date to 1 day after — because sperm can survive in the body for up to 5 days.
ovulationPage.accuracyText: The calendar method gives a useful estimate for women with regular cycles, but stress, illness, travel and hormonal shifts can move ovulation earlier or later. For a more precise picture, combine it with ovulation tests, basal body temperature tracking, or cervical mucus observation.
ovulationPage.signsTitle: What are the signs of ovulation?

signs.title: Changes in cervical mucus
signs.text: Clear, stretchy discharge resembling egg white is the clearest sign of your most fertile days.

signs.title: A rise in basal body temperature
signs.text: Temperature rises by about 0.3–0.5°C after ovulation and stays elevated until your next period.

signs.title: Mild one-sided pelvic pain
signs.text: Some women feel a light twinge on one side, known as "mittelschmerz".

signs.title: Increased libido
signs.text: A natural rise in sex drive can be your body's signal that it's preparing for a fertile window.

signs.title: Breast tenderness
signs.text: Hormonal shifts can make breasts feel slightly tender or fuller.

faq.q: Can an ovulation calculator be used as birth control?
faq.a: No. The calculator gives a statistical estimate, not a contraception method. If you want to avoid pregnancy, discuss reliable contraception options with your doctor.

faq.q: Will the calculator work if my cycle is irregular?
faq.a: The estimate is less reliable for irregular cycles, since the method relies on a fairly stable cycle length. In that case, ovulation tests or a doctor's guidance are more reliable.

faq.q: How many days before or after ovulation can I conceive?
faq.a: The fertile window opens about 5 days before ovulation and closes 1 day after it, because sperm can survive in the body for several days.

faq.q: Is ovulation always painless?
faq.a: Most women feel no symptoms at all, and that's completely normal. Others notice mild pelvic pain or a change in discharge.

faq.q: How can I track this more precisely over time?
faq.a: Anacan's Flow mode sharpens your personal predictions with every cycle you log, and factoring in your symptoms narrows the fertile window further.

symptomsPage.title: Pregnancy Symptoms: How to Recognize the First Signs
symptomsPage.subtitle: 12 early pregnancy symptoms that can appear even before your missed period — and how to tell them apart from PMS.
symptomsPage.intro: The earliest pregnancy symptoms usually start 6–12 days after fertilization, around implantation. The most common are a missed period, breast tenderness, fatigue, nausea, frequent urination and heightened smell sensitivity. None of these symptoms is 100% conclusive on its own — a pregnancy test is the only reliable confirmation.

list.title: Missed period
list.text: The most reliable early signal, especially if your cycle is usually regular.

list.title: Breast tenderness and swelling
list.text: Hormonal shifts can make breasts feel sore or heavy.

list.title: Fatigue
list.text: A rapid rise in progesterone causes strong tiredness in the early weeks.

list.title: Morning sickness
list.text: Usually starts around week 6 and can strike at any time of day.

list.title: Frequent urination
list.text: Increased blood volume makes the kidneys work harder.

list.title: Implantation bleeding or cramping
list.text: Light spotting when the fertilized egg attaches to the uterine wall.

list.title: Sensitivity to smell and taste
list.text: Ordinary smells can suddenly feel overwhelming.

list.title: Changes in appetite
list.text: Sudden aversions to certain foods or strong cravings can appear.

list.title: Dizziness
list.text: Can be caused by shifts in blood pressure and blood sugar.

list.title: Basal body temperature stays elevated
list.text: Unlike a typical luteal phase, temperature stays high past the expected period date.

symptomsPage.comparisonIntro: Many early pregnancy symptoms overlap with PMS, which is exactly what makes the first weeks confusing. The table below highlights the key differences:

comparison.p: Continues after your period would have started

comparison.m: Appears before your period, then fades

symptomsPage.whenTestTitle: When should you take a pregnancy test?
symptomsPage.whenTestText: For the most accurate result, test on or after the first day of your missed period — by then hCG levels in urine are high enough to detect reliably. If you want to test earlier, choose a high-sensitivity test (10 mIU/ml) with your first morning urine, and repeat in a few days if the result is negative.
symptomsPage.whenDoctorTitle: When should you see a doctor?
symptomsPage.whenDoctorText: If your test is positive, contact your doctor as soon as possible to register your pregnancy. Seek emergency care immediately if you experience severe abdominal pain, heavy bleeding, or shoulder pain alongside these symptoms — these can be signs of an ectopic pregnancy.

faq.q: Do all women experience the same symptoms?
faq.a: No. Every body is different — some women conceive without noticing any symptoms at all, while others experience several at once. Having no symptoms does not mean you're not pregnant.

faq.q: How many days before a missed period can symptoms start?
faq.a: Some women notice mild symptoms shortly after implantation (6–12 days after fertilization), but most symptoms become clearer after the missed period.

faq.q: Can you be pregnant without nausea?
faq.a: Yes, completely possible and normal. Roughly a third of pregnant women never experience nausea at all.

faq.q: How can I tell implantation bleeding apart from a period?
faq.a: Implantation bleeding is usually lighter, paler in color, and lasts 1–2 days, without the increasing flow typical of a normal period.

faq.q: My test was negative but symptoms continue — what should I do?
faq.a: Retest in 3–5 days with your first morning urine. If symptoms persist or worry you, contact your doctor.
